First development release of 0.17.0. Everything below is meant to ship in v0.17.0 once it survives a test pass - install this to help catch what doesn't, and expect a v0.17.0-dev2 when it does.

### Highlights

- **Service level agreements.** Governance → Monitoring → SLAs: an agreement promises an availability target over a month, quarter, year or a rolling 7, 30 or 90 days, inside service hours and outside holidays, provided for the tenant, some of its sites or locations, a contact or a name. Members are devices, VMs, addresses, prefixes (the monitored addresses in them) and circuits (measured on the addresses cabled to their ends, or on a monitor address such as the carrier's far-end gateway), in check groups that say which checks count; devices can also join by selector (site, role, type, platform, tag, name pattern). A redundancy group counts a pair as one unit, and units combine as *Average*, *Worst member* or *All must be up*. Figures come from the status-change history, are stored per period, recomputed every 15 minutes and frozen seven days after the period ends; counting rules are revisioned, so a closed period keeps the rules it ran under. Exclusions take time out with a required reason, and planned maintenance on a member's device or circuit can be left out. **New agreement** is a three-step wizard - the agreement, its members, then the checks that count, pre-ticked from what the members already run. A viewer limited to some sites gets a partial figure over what they may see.
- **SLA analysis, alerts, credits and reports.** An agreement's Overview computes any period or date range live, per day or hour, sliced by check group, site, check type, redundancy group or member: availability with an hourly drill-down, the error budget burning down, where the down time went, a weekday × hour heatmap, incident lengths, latency, a members-by-check matrix of availability pills and a strip per member, with the last twelve periods as pills above and a **forecast** for the open period. Breached, at risk, low coverage and latency alerts go to any notification channel once per period, and two **burn-rate alerts** (fast: 1 h and 5 min at 14.4x; slow: 6 h and 30 min at 6x, both editable) catch a sharp outage early in the month, checked every minute. **Latency objectives** - *99% of ICMP probes within 20 ms* - get their own figure, budget and alert. **Service credits** price tiers, a fee and a currency into every period, behind a new *view credits* permission. Period reports download as PDF or CSV, are emailed when a period freezes or with **Email report** to any address, and an overview report covers every agreement; the SLAs list's **Last 12** column counts the finished periods that met the target.
- **SLA and availability columns.** Device, VM, IP address, prefix, circuit, site and cluster lists gain an **SLA** column - the object's strictest agreement against its target, filterable by state - and an **Availability** column over a window you pick (the tenant default is a new monitoring setting), with "68% measured" when part of it went unmeasured. A provider's Circuits tab has both. An object's Monitoring tab (a circuit's Overview) lists its agreements with **Add to SLA**, and the device selection bar adds many at once.
- **The topology Diagram.** Maps → Topology opens on a new **Diagram** tab: one card per device filled with its role's colour, the name bold, a status or monitoring pill in the corner and a few **card lines** under it (IP, loopback, serial, custom fields - set under Settings → Topology for all devices or per role, at tenant or deployment level, per saved view from Display, and per device on its form). **Detailed** gives every cabled interface its own nub and named cable, **Simple** one line per device pair with a `2x` count. Lines are **Straight**, **Elbow** (laned, routed round the cards), **Bendy** (curves that keep the shape drawn while dragging and part where several leave one point; a line no curve gets clear of a card goes round it as an Elbow) or **Cyclical** (arcs round the cards between), for the view or one link at a time. **Link labels** put the shared subnet on the line's chip and each end's port and address on its own cable. Breakout cables draw as one trunk splitting into legs. **Photo** draws a device as its type's front photo with each cable on the port it is plugged into, or at the photo's edge with **Display ▸ Cables to** *Edge* (also per device). **Bands** (Arrange ▸ Bands by role or device type) stack the map into titled layers that can hold several roles, merge and split, with side bands down the right; **notes** add text, cloud, globe or building markers. **New view** starts from a blank canvas or the map on screen, and devices are dragged in from a device list. Wiring and Flat are folded into Detailed and Simple. (#164)
- **Diagram exports.** One Export menu saves the map as **PNG**, **SVG**, **PDF** (A4, A3, Letter or Tabloid, landscape or portrait, rendered on the server with a title block) or an editable **draw.io** file - as shown on screen by default, or Simple or Detailed; cards linked back to Danbyte, elbows on draw.io's own router, bands as swimlanes, LLDP and BGP on their own layers - and **Print** opens the PDF ready to print. Files are drawn from the map's data, not the screen, for the whole map or the visible area, with an optional title and legend. The Hierarchy and Logical tabs, Virtual topology, trace maps and a tunnel's map export the same way. (#164)
- **Monitoring history that outlives the raw results.** A new `danbyte-rollups` timer keeps hourly records per check (30 days) and daily ones for good: time in each state, incidents, latency percentiles, spikes against the check's own baseline and a latency histogram. Each check gets **its own page** with availability, p50/p95/p99, baseline and spikes over 24 hours to a year. Monitoring gains **Explore** (checks grouped by site, role, device type, platform, device, prefix, VRF, check or check kind, worst first) and **Latency** (per check kind, the checks furthest from their normal and with the most spikes), and the Checks list gains 7-day availability, p95 and baseline columns. Latency charts draw one check kind at a time instead of mixing pings with HTTPS fetches.
- **Named dashboards.** Beside your own dashboard, build named ones - "Aarhus DC", the NOC wall - each with its own layout, time frame, refresh interval and scope (sites, regions, roles, device types, tags, SLAs), shared with the tenant or with groups. Anyone who can see one can duplicate it or open it as their dashboard; every widget loads with the viewer's permissions. New widgets for one SLA, all SLAs, availability by group, slowest against normal, coverage and open maintenance, and a **TV** mode that cycles through several dashboards on a wall display.
- **Every field is a column.** A table's Columns menu lists what is shown and, in sections, everything else its rows carry - fields, related objects one step out (a device's **Region**, location, rack, platform, primary, secondary and OOB IP, config template) and every custom field - hidden until ticked, sortable and exported. Drag to reorder and press **Save** to keep the layout - changes no longer save as you make them, and closing the menu without Save drops them. (#243)

### Security

- **Operator and Read-only no longer reach users, groups and permissions.** *All object types* used to include them, so an Operator could open user management and the Admin pages and edit groups and grants to give itself more, and Read-only could read every account and grant. It now covers every type except those three; a grant reaches them only by naming them, and such a grant takes no site limit or row constraint. The Administrator group's grant names them. Holding *change* on Users is what opens the Admin pages and tenant settings (and the deployment settings when the grant is not limited to tenants), so Operators - SSO and LDAP mappings onto Operator included - no longer see those, and only people who can manage users may share a named dashboard with a group they are not in. Permissions can no longer be staged or applied through a planned change, including a plan staged before the upgrade. How existing grants are rewritten is under Upgrading.
- **People pickers without user administration.** Notification subscriptions, script sharing, a site editor's viewer invite, task assignees and user or group custom fields list everyone who can work in the tenant and their groups, without their email address (shown only to people who may view users) and without needing access to Users. A spreadsheet import resolves person and group cells against the same list, so Operators can re-import their own exports.
- **Export and label templates stay inside the tenant.** A relation hands a template only this tenant's rows the user may view; users, groups and the tenant show a name at most; a lookup or ordering names one field of the row. Accounts, groups and grants can no longer be a template's subject. Templates that filtered or ordered through a relation, called `values`/`values_list`, or printed an owner's email or groups now render nothing or fail with a security error.
- **Sign-in mail.** Invites, password-reset links and emailed sign-in codes go through a tenant's own mail server only for accounts that work in that tenant alone; those for superusers, deployment administrators and people in several tenants go through the deployment's mail server, so a tenant admin cannot read them from their relay. An install with no deployment mail server still sends them through the tenant's - set up deployment email to keep them out of tenant relays.
- **Script sharing** accepts only people and groups of the script's tenant; superusers and deployment admins may pick anyone.
- **Other reads follow the reader's access:** custom-field object labels resolve only objects the caller may view, and nothing without an active tenant; compliance's affected rows need view on the object type and are cut to its sites; a virtual network lists only the VMs the caller may view.

### Monitoring & SLAs

- **Exclude an address from monitoring.** A switch on the IP's Monitoring tab parks every check on it - its own and inherited, on the core, on Outposts and Zabbix checks - closes its alerts, refuses *Check now*, and leaves it out of every count, digest and flapping list. An **Excluded** pill shows on the address, the prefix's address list, the device and the Checks list, which gains an Excluded facet. Excluded time is not measured in SLAs. The optional reason goes to the change log and journal. Only checks stop: SNMP polling, Redfish, watched endpoints, discovery sweeps and Zabbix's own polling of the host carry on. Outposts need no update.
- **Reset availability** for an address reused by a new host, from now or a date, with a **required reason**: uptime, strips and SLA figures count from then, the history is kept and shown as not counted, and a line on the tab reads *Availability reset by bob on 12 Sep 2026 14:05: New host on the address*. A period that had closed before the reset stays as it closed, a frozen one never changes, and a reset that touches an agreement needs change on it.
- API: `POST /api/monitoring/ips/<id>/exclude/` and `/reset-availability/`, and `?monitoring_excluded=` on the IP list. The IP API refuses changes to the exclusion and reset fields and points at those endpoints.
- **Holiday calendars** are edited on a twelve-month view: click days, name them, mark fixed dates as **Every year**, paste dates and ranges or open an .ics file, with Undo for an import. The list shows each calendar's days this year and the agreements that use it. Days run from 1970 to 2099; the API's `dates` is a list of `{date, name, yearly}` and still takes plain date strings.
- Charts: the hover follows the pointer instead of the first repeated label, the running day is drawn half filled, hours follow the 24-hour clock setting, and dashboard donuts, gauges, alert bars, latency and the SLA budget bar open the page behind them. Low coverage outlines the SLA badge instead of fading it.

### Topology & maps

- **One Maps menu.** Maps lists Site map, Floor plans, Topology and Virtual topology (formerly Virtualization → Network topology); the map tiles settings page is now Settings → Site map. The three maps share their toolbar parts, one **Objects** sidebar (search, All / Down / Degraded / Up tabs with counts, status pills, colour badges on group headers, Show all), one unsaved-changes dialog, an **Edited** badge and the shared loader, and the site map's legend matches the topology map's. The site map and floor plans' **View** menu is now **Display**, the topology and floor plan bars move what doesn't fit into **More**, and cable types read as the cable list names them.
- **Controls moved.** Layout direction and **Levels…** are under **Arrange ▸ Layout**; the header Levels button and Display's Layout section are gone. Hierarchy's Add device dialog is gone - devices come from the device list. Every tab uses the same words: *Hand-picked map* (formerly custom map), *Find on map*, *Reset layout*, *Color by* and *LAG bundles*.
- **Default view.** A star beside the Views select sets the saved view a bare /topology opens for the whole tenant, for tenant admins or holders of the new *set default* permission on topology views. Links from sites, devices and cables still open No view, and `?view=none` always does. A link to a deleted view says *View not found* and opens No view instead of the whole tenant under a blank select.
- **Saved views are documents.** Every drag, band, note, hide and reset is an undo step (up to 100, Ctrl/Cmd+Z to undo, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y to redo, and Undo and Redo buttons), Ctrl/Cmd+S saves, leaving with unsaved edits asks first, and a save over someone else's newer save is refused with **Save as…** or **Reload**. Deleting a view asks first. The change log records which parts of a view changed and their size instead of copying layouts of up to 8 MB.
- **Hide one line.** Right-click a line for *Open cable*, its own line type and *Hide* (H), which works on a single cable, bundle, LLDP neighbour or BGP session; a hidden line has its own eye in the sidebar. Right-click menus use the app's menus, bands and zones can be renamed from theirs, and zoom buttons replace the canvas controls.
- **Hierarchy, Logical and the other maps draw the Diagram's cards.** Hierarchy card headers are Diagram cards, and devices can be dropped onto it from the device list. The Logical tab, Virtual topology and a VM's Topology card share one rail diagram with role-coloured cards, VLAN status pills and dashed VMs, every element reachable with Tab. A device's Map tab, cable and interface trace maps (ordered along the run, a patch panel between its two ends) and a tunnel's Map tab are Diagram cards with Elbow lines; a run that dead-ends carries an **Incomplete** badge.
- **Big maps stay usable.** The Diagram is laid out in a web worker so a big site never holds the page, sorting a 2,400-device site into levels takes about 0.1 s instead of 2.5-5 s, only the cards in view are mounted, devices with no cable pack into a grid under the wired map, a map too big to fit opens on its busiest device at a readable zoom with a **Partial map** chip, the minimap paints large maps on one canvas, and the Objects list renders only what is scrolled into view. Large Hierarchy maps are laid out per island instead of growing off the canvas.
- API: `/api/topology/` also takes a POST body for large device sets and `include=card,link_ips,photo`; `/api/devices/?picker=palette` is the device list's light feed; `/api/topology-views/default/` reads and sets the default view; `POST /api/topology/export/pdf/` renders a diagram SVG as PDF.

### IPAM & DCIM

- **VLAN status** - Active, Reserved and Deprecated join the status catalog for VLANs, Active the default for new ones; the list shows and filters by it, bulk edit sets it. (#172)
- **Wi-Fi security modes** - WPA2, WPA3 and WPA2/WPA3 transition modes for Personal (WPA3-Personal is SAE) and Enterprise, Enhanced Open (OWE), a GCMP-256 cipher and a PMF field with its own column and filter. Combinations that don't fit the mode are refused and the form offers only what fits; switching to a mode without a passphrase removes the stored one, after the form says so. (#177)
- **Routing on virtual machines** - static routes and BGP, OSPF, IS-IS and EIGRP instances run on a device or a VM, with a Routing tab on the VM and the same `routing` block in its config template render. VTEPs and LDP stay device-only, and BGP sessions to or from a VM do not draw on the topology map. (#217)
- **Import from library** on the Module types and Rack types pages; rack-type files from the devicetype-library import as rack types. Each file needs add on the kind it creates, checked again when a folder runs in the background. (#182)
- **Bulk marker colour and icon** - tick sites, regions or locations and Edit: sites and locations take a marker colour and icon, regions a colour. The Locations list gains row selection. (#183)
- **Space map drill-down.** A block holding smaller child prefixes is drawn partly used, a rose bar where each child sits, and zooms in on click; a used block offers Open and Zoom into; a free block opens a menu - *Zoom into*, and *New child prefix here* and *Register an IP here* when you may add them - instead of going straight to the new-prefix form. Amber now marks an IP range, as a strip along the chip; stray IPs show as a count on a green chip. The zoom path is in the address, so Back and reload keep it.
- **Names with numbers sort as you count** - DIMM 2 before DIMM 10, Ethernet1/2 before Ethernet1/10 - in list endpoints, related lists, rendered routing config, table header clicks, trees, facets and legends, the same in every browser language. (#244)
- **Spec sheets read RAM in GB** whether a BMC sync recorded a DIMM in binary units or the form in decimal GB, so 32 sticks of 32 GB total 1024 GB; VM memory reads in GB too, and parts, modules and inventory are listed by slot then name. Mixed disks and memory read `2 × 2 TB · 8 × 10 TB` on the spec sheet and the Hardware tab instead of ten times the most common size. (#244)
- Devices, racks and VMs carry their site's region on every row, and device components carry `custom_fields` through the API. (#243)

### Everyday interface

- The colour picker's preset grid is one column per hue and five rows of shades, and fits short screens. (#184)
- Status history widget names are as wide as the longest name, up to half the widget, before they truncate.
- The filter expression builder keeps fields named like ids that hold values (`vlan_id`) and filters by site region; saving or deleting a custom field refreshes forms and list columns at once. (#243)
- API: `GET /api/list-fields/?path=` lists what a table's Columns menu offers; `/api/people/` and `/api/people/groups/` are the people pickers' lists.

### Faster lists

- A site-scoped user's permissions are loaded once per request instead of on every check (`/api/me/` from 178 to 25 queries), and the row-permission check no longer rebuilds the whole page for every row (with the IP list's own fix, a site-scoped list of 960 addresses went from 3.7 s to 0.9 s). The statuses list counts each status's use in one query instead of fourteen per status, and the IP address, VM interface, interface and port, cable, VM and object-permission lists no longer query per row. (#241)
- A saved topology view's map, LLDP links and BGP sessions are fetched once the view has loaded, not first for the whole tenant.

### Fixes

- The worst day in an availability chart drew no bar and read as unmeasured; the axis now sits below it.
- The alert list's silenced flag ignored silences scoped to a device.
- A layout saved with **Set as new-user default** was ignored, and new users got the built-in dashboard.
- Business hours on contacts and providers showed a clipped AM/PM under a 24-hour clock; they use the shared time picker, as SLA service hours do.
- The topology API answered a malformed id with a 500; it is a 400 now, and device sets are capped at 10,000 ids.
- A cable or status colour saved without its `#` painted nothing on the topology map.
- An uncabled port's trace offered *Left to right* and *Top to bottom* beside *Not cabled*.
- The Regions list's bulk bar offered Rename and Clone, which never worked there; they are gone.

### Upgrading

- **Expect a few minutes of retries while upgrading.** On a systemd install the upgraders put the new code in place before they run migrations and restart the services only at the end (after the interface build, for the git upgrader); a container install migrates before its new services start, but the old workers and scheduler run until they are replaced. Until then, timer runs and background jobs can fail and run again on the next tick, checks picked up in that window can wait up to ten minutes to run again, adding IP addresses can fail, and Administrator-group members who are not superusers have no user management until `auth_api.0024` has run. Nothing is written wrong, and it settles once everything has restarted. Upgrading by hand, stop the `danbyte-*` timers and the workers, run migrations, then start the new code.
- **Access grants are rewritten** (`auth_api.0024`-`0025`). Users, Groups and Permissions are named on the all-object grants that were administrator grants - view, add, change and delete limited neither to sites nor by rows, grants carrying *grant superuser*, and grants held only by the Administrator group - and taken off every other, including the built-in Operator and Read-only grants; the migration prints the grants it trimmed. If that would leave nobody able to manage users, the accounts that could get a grant of their own, *Kept user management (0.17 upgrade)*, and the top bar shows *After upgrade: 1 step* (Settings → Updates) until your administrators are in the Administrator group and that grant is gone.
- Migrations apply automatically: VLAN status and its statuses, Wi-Fi security, device card lines, natural component ordering and IP monitoring exclusion and reset (`api.0178`-`0183`), access types (`auth_api.0024`-`0025`), named dashboards, card-line settings and the default topology view (`core.0055`-`0057`), rollups, SLAs and their alerts, reports, burn rules, circuits, credits, latency histograms and objectives (`monitoring.0094`-`0103`), and routing on VMs (`routing.0013`).
- `danbyte-rollups` (every 5 minutes), `danbyte-sla` (every 15 minutes) and `danbyte-sla-burn` (every minute) are new timers; the upgraders link and enable them, the installer sets them up on a fresh install, and the container's scheduler runs them. `MONITORING_ROLLUP_HOURLY_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 30) sets how long hourly rollups are kept.
- Rollups record from the upgrade on. `manage.py rollup_checks --backfill 90` builds them from the history already on disk; the latency histograms behind SLA latency objectives fill in for the last 27 days by themselves, a few days per run.
- Rendered configs may reorder once: component lists now come in natural order. (#244)
- Existing VLANs start without a status; tick them in the list and use Edit. Existing SSIDs keep their settings: WPA Personal, WPA Enterprise and WEP stay as legacy modes beside the new ones, and PMF starts blank.
- A topology view last shown on Wiring or Flat opens on the Diagram and brings its arrangement and zones across the first time, waiting for Save; the old arrangements stay in the view for one more release. Their cables keep the look they had: Wiring's routed cables become Elbow, Flat's curves Bendy. Old `?tab=wiring` and `?tab=flat` links open the Diagram in Detailed or Simple.
- Plugins: list pages get the new columns from the plugin's list serializer; mark getters only a detail page needs with `@detail_only`.
